subject: Follow-up: Post-demo notes — audit log export schema + residency & retention questions
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erika Solomon <erika.solomon@fairview.health>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@fairview.health>, marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: Post-demo notes — audit log export schema + residency & retention questions

Hi Erika —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today — appreciate the candid discussion about your operational needs. Quick recap and a couple of asks so we can scope the evidence pack for Fairview's security review: 

Summary of what we covered
- Who/When: you need a readable export that shows user/service identity, action (read/write/delete/etc.), resource identifier, timestamp, region/zone, and request correlation id.
- Retention: compliance team is asking for 3 years of immutable records plus a rolling 90-day low-latency export for incident triage.
- Residency: primary concern is that metadata about who accessed customer data must remain in US regions; export files can be stored in your GCS/Azure container in us-central.
- PII: you'd like guidance on whether we can deliver a filtered "who/when" export with tokenized identifiers (non-reversible hashes) to avoid transmitting customer PII in the evidence pack.

Requests from Fairview to us (so we are aligned):
1) Confirm an export schema (CSV/NDJSON) that includes minimal PII and a separate mapping file for hashed IDs under an approved exchange protocol.
2) Clarify retention windows we can demonstrate from our service (granularity: daily snapshots, and point-in-time recovery).
3) Provide a sample "who/when" CSV (anonymized) and the documentation we will submit to your auditors describing controls around log immutability and KMS keys.

Next steps from Redwood:
- I'll pull together a proposed export schema and a short sample (anonymized) by EOD tomorrow.
- I'll loop in Karthik from our security team to confirm KMS/HSM controls and whether we can provide signed manifests for immutability.

If there are any additional columns you need in the export (e.g., session_id, ttl, client_ip subnet), call them out and I'll add them to the schema.

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
Attachments: none in this message

From: Erika Solomon <erika.solomon@fairview.health>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@fairview.health>, compliance@fairview.health
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Post-demo notes — audit log export schema + residency & retention questions

Hi Grace —

Thanks for the recap — that captures the conversation well. A few clarifications from Compliance: 

1) For the purposes of our SOC/ISO submission we need exports in both CSV (for reviewers) and NDJSON (for ingestion into our SIEM). Can you confirm both will be supported?
2) Regarding PII: hashed IDs are acceptable if the hashing algorithm and salt are disclosed to our compliance team and we can provide a secondary process to reverse-map under an approved legal request. If redaction/tokenization is simpler that's fine too, but we need the traceability plan.
3) For retention evidence: we will accept a 3-year retention demonstration if you can provide immutable manifests signed by your KMS/HSM for each quarterly archive.
4) Residency: we will accept the export being delivered to our GCS bucket located in us-central1 but we require an audit trail showing that at-rest copies were not present in other regions during the snapshot period.

Can you also include a small sample of the "who/when" schema with at least one example of an API key/service principal entry vs. a human user entry (to show the distinction and associated attributes)? 

If you can get the sample and the schema to us by EOD your time tomorrow that would let us add it to the packet for our security review next Friday.

-Erika
Erika Solomon
Head of Compliance
Fairview Health Systems

---Original message quoted below---

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Erika Solomon <erika.solomon@fairview.health>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:58:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Post-demo notes — audit log export schema + residency & retention questions

Erika —

Thanks, understood. Attaching two artifacts: 
- rw_audit_export_schema_v1.md — a proposed schema outlining CSV/NDJSON columns and types, recommended hash approaches, and delivery options.
- sample_who_when_anon.csv — a one-page anonymized sample showing both service principal and user entries.

Quick notes on what we can provide immediately:
- Formats: we can produce both CSV and NDJSON exports on demand (scheduled or point-in-time) scoped to customer tenancy.
- PII handling: by default we include user_id and provider_identity; for evidence packs we can return user_display (redacted) and user_id hashed with HMAC-SHA256 using a per-customer salt under our KMS. We will include the KMS key id and signed manifest (RSASSA-PSS) for the archive.
- Retention proof: we can provide immutable quarterly archives (WORM-style) with manifest files signed by our HSM-backed key, plus a daily low-latency export for 90 days for triage.
- Residency: exports will be produced in the customer-specified region and written directly to your GCS bucket using customer-managed encryption keys (we support CMEK for GCS/Azure). We will include a delivery audit file showing the physical region and the source node id.

One open question for Fairview: when you say "not present in other regions during the snapshot period" — do you need us to run a cross-region scan and produce a signed attestation that no copies existed elsewhere, or is a signed delivery manifest + internal replication policy sufficient? If you need attestation we will have Karthik coordinate with our legal/security operations team to produce the statement (this may take an extra 3–5 business days). 

I'll follow up with Karthik to confirm the HSM signing flow and to draft a short attestation template if required.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- rw_audit_export_schema_v1.md (text/markdown stub)
- sample_who_when_anon.csv (text/csv stub)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Security Ops <security-ops@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Post-demo notes — audit log export schema + residency & retention questions

Team —

FYI: Fairview (RW-FT-4932) needs the following to close their compliance packet: 
- CSV + NDJSON export of "who/when" for a provided 90-day window (low-latency) and quarterly immutable archives for 3 years.
- Hashing approach: HMAC-SHA256 with per-customer salt stored in KMS. Fairview wants the ability to reverse-map via legal request; we need to confirm process & access controls.
- Signed manifests: RSASSA-PSS using HSM key; manifests must include archive checksum (SHA-256), generation timestamp, and origin region.
- Residency attestation: they asked whether a cross-region scan is required. I recommend we offer a signed attestation template (standard language) and only run scans on request due to cost. We should be explicit about eventual consistency of replication and our retention purge timelines.

Action items (owner in parentheses):
1) Produce the NDJSON/CSV export pipeline doc and include column names and example payloads (Grace — deliver by EOD tomorrow).
2) Confirm HSM signing workflow and provide KMS key ids + sample manifest (Karthik — I'll prepare a technical note and sample manifest by EOD two business days).
3) Legal to prepare attestation wording if Fairview requests a cross-region scan (Marissa — please loop in Legal).
4) Ops to confirm where export staging nodes reside and produce the short region-delivery proof we will include in the manifest (Security Ops — please provide a short canned paragraph).

I'll coordinate and we can package the two artifacts Grace attached plus the manifest and attestation as part of the evidence pack.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference
